newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-firm- dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-firm- dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Tuesday were seen steady-firm, possibly $0.50 per cwt higher on a reduction in hog supplies, livestock dealers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top hog prices could range $48.50 to $49.00 and Illinois top hog prices at the plant could range $47.50 to $48.50, with a chance at $49.00, they said.
Indiana and Ohio top prices for hogs at the plant could range $48.50 to $49.00, the dealers said.
Cash hog prices also were seen supported by ideas pork prices were near a bottom and set to go higher, they said.
Pork prices at midday, however, were mostly steady in light trading, the sources said.
Fresh hams at midday were steady for 17-20 lb cuts and steady-$1.00 lower for 20-26 lb hams, while pork bellies were steady to firm and lean trimmings steady, USDA reported.

Outlooks for lighter supplies of hogs the next three to four weeks would mean less pork production during that time, the dealers said. Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hog marketings on Friday totaled 90,000 head, below that day's estimate of 100,000. Saturday's receipts were 26,000, compared with the estimate of 20,000, USDA said.
Receipts Monday were pegged at 105,000 head, compared with 106,000 a week ago and year ago.
